c1.note: The 8-K says Merger Sub (KWA Investment Co.) merged into Monsanto, which survived as a wholly owned Bayer subsidiary. All variants match.

c2.note: The merger agreement is dated September 14, 2016.

c4.note: Bayer signed the agreement at $128 per share in September 2016.

c5.note: Section 4.1(a) sets the consideration at $128.00 per share in cash, without interest.

c7.note: Options and SARs convert into $128 less the exercise price, paid shortly after the Effective Time.

c8.note: The deal was widely reported at about $66 billion including net debt, and DOJ cites the $66 billion figure. The $128 per share was all cash.

c9.note: Bayer announced its intention to acquire Monsanto in May 2016. The first written proposal was May 10, 2016.

c10.note: Bayer closed the acquisition on June 7, 2018, and Monsanto shares left the NYSE. The roughly $63B figure includes debt.

c11.note: Bayer became the sole owner of Monsanto at closing.

c12.note: Monsanto asked the NYSE to suspend trading and delist its shares on the closing date, June 7, 2018.

c13.note: Bayer's closing release says shareholders are paid $128 per share. The 8-K confirms the cash conversion.

c16.note: Bayer stated ~$63B including Monsanto debt; closed June 7, 2018. Variants A, B and E are all consistent.

c19.note: DOJ release of May 29, 2018 says 'proposed $66 billion acquisition of Monsanto'.

c21.note: DOJ on May 29, 2018 required ~$9B of divestitures, to BASF.

c22.note: DOJ quote says the BASF divestiture will fully resolve all horizontal and vertical competition concerns.

c23.note: DOJ lists cotton, canola, soybean and vegetable seed businesses and Liberty herbicide.

c26.note: Bayer release says divested businesses had €2.2B 2017 sales and a €7.6B base price; BASF as buyer is confirmed elsewhere.

c27.note: Bayer and DOJ materials identify BASF as the divestiture buyer.

c28.note: EC conditionally approved on March 21, 2018 with remedies of about €6B+; the date and amount match my knowledge, though the passages only confirm March 2018.

c29.note: EC remedies covered seeds and pesticides overlaps, R&D, and digital agriculture licensing, per the EC press release (IP/18/2282).

c30.note: Monsanto 8-K cites the court-mandated hold separate period; Bayer says integration follows completion of the BASF divestments.

c31.note: Bayer's Q2 2018 release refers to businesses divested to BASF in August 2018; the August 1 and 16 closing dates match what I know.

c32.note: Bayer said integration would begin after the BASF divestments, and it began on August 16, 2018, as I know it.

c33.note: The June 7, 2018 release says integration could happen once the BASF divestments were complete and was expected to start in about two months.

c34.note: DOJ required about $9B in divestitures to BASF as a condition of the deal.

c36.note: The June 4, 2018 release states Bayer remains the company name, Monsanto will no longer be a company name, and brands are retained. All three variants are accurate.

c39.note: The Q3 2026 statement (published Nov 3, 2026) covers legacy Monsanto Roundup litigation and the Monsanto entity's settlement obligations. The Monsanto entity persists as a Bayer subsidiary.

c40.note: Bayer acquired Monsanto for $128 per share and became its sole owner; this was an acquisition, not a merger of equals.

c41.note: The release calls it the largest acquisition in the company's history.

c42.note: Widely reported as the largest all-cash takeover on record; no saved passage states it, but I know it from reporting at the time.

c43.note: The June 4, 2018 release summary says the deal would double the size of the agriculture business.

c44.note: The 2016 deal announcement says growers will benefit from a broad set of solutions across seeds and traits, digital agriculture and crop protection.

c45.note: Bayer's 2016 announcement described pairing its crop protection portfolio, including biologicals, with Monsanto's seeds and traits.

c46.note: Bayer's June 24, 2020 release states total payment of $10.1-10.9 billion (EUR 9.1-9.8 billion) for Roundup litigation.

c47.note: Release states ~75% of ~125,000 filed and unfiled claims; no-admission wording is standard and consistent with Bayer's later disclosures.

c48.note: Release: up to $400 million for dicamba drift litigation.

c49.note: Release summary: most PCB water litigation exposure for approximately $820 million.

c50.note: Release names free cash flow and Animal Health divestment (plus surplus liquidity and bonds) as funding sources.

c51.note: Bayer's annual report states the February 2026 proposed nationwide class settlement for current and future NHL claims.

c52.note: The annual report did say a motion was filed, but the settlement was preliminarily approved in March 2026, so 'still awaiting' is not current.

c53.note: The settlement was announced in February 2026 but preliminary approval came in March 2026, not February.

c54.note: Q3 2026 report: preliminary approval March 2026; settlement not final and effective until final approval and all appeals are exhausted.

c55.note: Report states declining capped annual payments for up to 21 years totaling up to US$7.25 billion; not final until appeals concluded.

c57.note: Report states the February 2026 settlement agreements contain no admission of liability or wrongdoing.

c58.note: Bloomberg on June 12, 2026 said a fairness hearing was scheduled; it was later held Sept 14, so this is historical.

c59.note: Reuters Sept 14, 2026: Monsanto urged Judge Timothy Boyer to approve the settlement at the final approval hearing; the ruling is still pending.

c60.note: Reuters: proposed settlement offers payouts from $10,000 to $165,000.

c61.note: Reuters said the judge did not indicate when he would rule, and the Nov 2026 recap says a ruling is still expected before Christmas, so he has not ruled.

c62.note: Reuters quotes Monsanto attorney Bennett saying this at the Sept 14 hearing.

c63.note: Recap reports CEO Anderson expects a ruling before Christmas.

c65.note: Bayer's press release dated June 25, 2026 states the 7:2 ruling and the FIFRA preemption holding.

c67.note: The release says the decision 'helps to bring significant containment to the Roundup litigation'.

c68.note: The ruling addresses failure-to-warn claims, and AP notes it could still allow other suits (design-defect claims, per the attorney Keller context); Bayer says failure-to-warn claims are the vast majority of cases.

c69.note: Reuters says the litigation has weighed on Bayer since the 2018 acquisition, costing billions and driving down its share price.

c70.note: AP states about 200,000 claims have been made in total, while about 65,000 are pending.

c71.note: AP says Bayer previously set aside $16 billion to settle cases.

c72.note: Reuters and the TradingView recap both say about 65,000 claims.

c73.note: Bloomberg of June 12, 2026 cites a more than $60 billion wipeout in market value since the Monsanto purchase eight years ago.

c75.note: The 2020 settlement was about $10.1-10.9B, and later provisions (the $16B set aside, plus the $7.25B proposal) exceed it, though the passages do not state the total charges directly.

c64.note: The saved PBS source confirms that objectors challenged the $675M attorneys' fee request. Search coverage of the Sept 2026 fairness hearing says more than 100 class members and about a dozen health plans filed objections, with the health plans worried about lien and subrogation rights. That coverage

c74.note: Many outlets call the deal one of the worst acquisitions. Examples are Fierce Pharma ('worst deal ever'), the Wall Street Journal ranking it with AOL-Time Warner and Bank of America-Countrywide, MoneyWeek, and AgroPages ('top 3 worst deals'). c9.note: Bayer made its unsolicited offer for Monsanto in May 2016 (PharmTech; Bayer press). The definitive $128/share agreement followed in September 2016.

c25.note: The DOJ release lists the cotton, canola, soybean and vegetable seed businesses, Liberty herbicide, seed treatments, IP and research/pipeline R&D, and digital agriculture.

c35.note: Under the DOJ's conditional approval, integration could start once the BASF divestments were done. Until then Monsanto operated independently.

c48.note: Bayer's June 24, 2020 release says it would pay up to $400M to resolve the dicamba drift MDL.

c55.note: Bayer's Q3 2026 statement gives the declining capped payments for up to 21 years, up to US$7.25B. It says the settlement isn't final until appeals end. I found no report of final approval after the Sept 14 hearing.

c62.note: The Euronext/Reuters report quotes Monsanto counsel Bennett at the hearing: 'This is the settlement. There is not another settlement.'

c66.note: PBS, Jun 25, 2026: the Supreme Court ruled 7-2 that federal law preempts state failure-to-warn claims over Roundup (Durnell).

c68.note: PBS says the ruling is about failure-to-warn claims. The plaintiff's attorney said design-defect suits could still go ahead, and Bayer said only failure-to-warn cases should be dismissed.
